summary.intent: Deploy v0.25.0 to staging after merging the release PR, then investigate and fix performance and auth issues discovered during smoke testing.
summary.outcome: Unblocked staging deployment via v0.25.1 (fixing a broken Dockerfile and release-please config), triggered Tag Staging Release, and identified root causes for slow IPNS publish and broken token refresh — with the IPNS fix in a merged PR and a larger HTTP client consolidation refactor delegated to a subagent.

repo: Staging deployment does not auto-trigger on release tags — it requires a manual 'Tag Staging Release' workflow dispatch that runs E2E tests and creates a v*-staging-rc-* tag.
release-please with a multi-package config requires `${component}` in `pull-request-title-pattern`; omitting it causes 'untagged merged release PRs' abort on subsequent runs.
The API is intentionally zero-knowledge (no plaintext/crypto ops), so apps/api has no workspace package dependencies — the stale packages/crypto COPY in the Dockerfile was purely leftover.

The web app has three distinct HTTP client paths: orval react-query fetch client (custom-instance.ts), hand-written axios client (lib/api/client.ts), and IPFS functions (lib/api/ipfs.ts). Token refresh only existed on the axios path.
The web app generates ~8,812 lines of react-query hooks via its own orval config but uses actual hooks from only 1 endpoint (health check); everything else imports the raw generated functions.
`@cipherbox/api-client` (axios-functions orval mode) exists for non-React consumers; the web app duplicates generation in react-query mode but derives minimal benefit.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instances hibernate and return HTTP 503 with 'instance is loading' on first deploy hit — transient, not a real failure.
`chore` commits do not trigger release-please version bumps; only `fix` and `feat` do.

code.finding: The `result` variable was being mutated to 'delegated_error' on DHT publish failure. After the fire-and-forget fix this no longer mutates, correctly reflecting that the DB write (the meaningful operation) succeeded.

Had a stale COPY for packages/crypto/package.json that the API does not depend on. With the expanded pnpm workspace package list this caused `pnpm deploy` to fail looking for @cipherbox/core (a transitive dep of crypto).
pull-request-title-pattern was set to `chore: release` without `${component}`, breaking release-please's ability to match merged PRs back to components in a multi-package repo.
Uses raw fetch() with no 401 handling — token refresh interceptor only existed on the axios client, leaving all orval react-query hook calls unrecovered on access token expiry.
Separate orval config generating react-query client mode directly into apps/web/src/api/. Parallel to packages/api-client which generates axios-functions mode — duplication with minimal benefit.

workflow: When release-please gets stuck with 'untagged merged release PRs', manually creating the git tag and GitHub release from the correct commit unblocks subsequent runs.
The Tag Staging Release workflow checkouts the release tag commit, so any hotfix must be in a new tagged version — you cannot patch staging without cutting a new release.
Fire-and-forget async operations (DHT publish) should not block API responses when the authoritative state (DB) has already been updated successfully.
Subagent isolation is effective for debug investigations that burn context fast — spawning separate agents per issue keeps the main context lean.

friction: Staging deployment silently did not kick off after release PR merge — the manual Tag Staging Release workflow was forgotten, requiring investigation to rediscover.
release-please aborted on v0.25.1 due to missing `${component}` in title pattern — a non-obvious config requirement for multi-package repos that was only surfaced after the fact.
Dockerfile build failure with expanded package list was a stale artifact from a previous dependency, causing the staging pipeline to fail before the root cause was clear.
Transient Grafana Cloud 503 during deployment caused a misleading job failure that required log investigation to identify as non-critical.
Token refresh breakage was only discovered through an unrelated long-running batch operation — not caught during normal short-session testing.
open_items: PR #307 (release-please title pattern fix) needs to be merged to prevent the same abort on future releases.
PR #308 (IPNS fire-and-forget fix) needs CI to pass and be merged, then v0.25.1 staging deploy needs to complete.

Web app HTTP client consolidation refactor: delete apps/web/src/api/ and orval config, migrate all imports to @cipherbox/api-client, eliminate lib/api/client.ts, centralize token refresh in the api-client package. Delegated to subagent at end of session.

Token refresh fix (shared token-refresh.ts across all three client paths) was stashed as it will be superseded by the consolidation refactor — needs to be re-applied or incorporated into the refactor.
@cipherbox/api-client needs withCredentials: true and a 401 refresh interceptor before it can fully replace the web app's fetch client.
